key_insight: Embed neural networks as unknown functional components inside PDEs and train them on observational data so the networks converge to the true unknown functions, enabling recovery of function-valued coefficients from data with high accuracy.
problem_solved: Many PDE models contain unknown spatially or temporally varying functions (e.g., coefficients, sources) that are hard or impossible to measure directly; prior workflows focus on scalar parameters, not full functions—this work provides a practical method to infer those functions from data.
method: Represent each unknown function in the PDE by a neural network whose input is space/time (and optionally solution features) and whose output is the function value.
Embed the neural networks into the PDE solver or physics-informed loss; combine data-misfit and PDE-consistency terms to form a differentiable loss.
Train end-to-end with gradient-based optimization so the networks adapt to reproduce observed solution data and satisfy the PDE, recovering the underlying functions.
impact: Enables practitioners to recover spatially/temporally varying model components directly from data, improving prediction and interpretability of physics-based ML models; lowers the barrier to fusing domain knowledge with flexible learnable components in scientific ML.
visual_elements: Schematic: PDE block diagram showing unknown function replaced by a neural network (NN icon inside PDE).
Training loop infographic: observed data → loss (data + PDE residual) → backprop → updated NN, iterated until convergence.
Comparison plots: true vs. recovered function (line or heatmap) and corresponding PDE solution before/after recovery.
Error/residual heatmap or convergence curve showing decreasing PDE residual and data-mismatch during training.
paper_title: Learning functional components of PDEs from data using neural networks
paper_authors: Torkel E. Loman, Yurij Salmaniw, Antonio Leon Villares, Jose A. Carrillo, Ruth E. Baker
